title: 34.6 A 47.3-to-58.4GHz Differential Quasi-Class-E Colpitts Oscillator Achieving 198.8dBc/Hz FoMT
problem: Millimeter-wave communication systems (5G, satellite) require local-oscillation signals with exceptionally high spectral purity (low phase noise and spurs). Traditional mm-wave VCOs suffer limited performance; harmonic-extraction approaches require power-hungry amplification stages; multi-core coupling topologies achieve only 190–191dB FoM(T), falling 5–10dB short of low-frequency counterparts.
motivation: Complex modulation schemes for high data-rate mm-wave transmission necessitate ultra-pure LO signals; phase noise and spur degradation directly limit spectral efficiency and system performance.
method: The design starts with a quasi-class-E Colpitts oscillator—a circuit that generates oscillating signals using capacitors and inductors while minimizing wasted energy—and adds a transformer-based two-port resonance structure (a transformer with two connection points tuned to create strong feedback at specific frequencies). This combination achieves very high-frequency operation across 47.3–58.4GHz while reducing phase noise—unwanted random timing variations in the signal—directly within the circuit through careful waveform shaping. Implemented in 40-nanometer CMOS technology, it achieves phase noise of -124.9 to -119.8dBc/Hz at 10MHz offset.
key_novelty: The core innovation is a transformer-based two-port resonance structure in a quasi-class-E Colpitts oscillator that surpasses previous designs using harmonic extraction (frequency multiples) or coupled oscillators, achieving a figure-of-merit score of 198.8dBc/Hz.
contributions: Peak FoM of 192.3dBc/Hz and FoM(T) of 198.8dBc/Hz in 47.3–58.4GHz range
Phase noise suppression via transformer-based resonance achieving -124.9 to -119.8dBc/Hz at 10MHz
5–10dB improvement over prior harmonic-extraction and multi-core designs
Efficient waveform shaping reducing power dissipation while maintaining phase noise performance

metrics.other: Phase noise: -124.9 to -119.8dBc/Hz @ 10MHz, FoM(T): 198.8dBc/Hz, Tuning range: 47.3–58.4GHz

primary_theme: Ultra-low-phase-noise mm-wave VCO via transformer-based quasi-class-E architecture
